text.p: These are the major headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Michel Gauthier to quit as leader of separatist Bloc Quebecois: Internal fighting forces resignation; party faces convention before election.
- Let police review own acts, Ontario report says: Six-week study wants less civilian input.
- Russian military unrest growing: Bid to fire general triggers new row.
- Canadian Airlines seeking to suspend debt payments: Plan would free up $170 million to keep planes flying.
- Boutros-Ghali's hopes for second term wane: African leaders urged to nominate others from continent for top UN post.
- Placer Dome enters Bre-X fray: Vancouver company aims to break up Barrick's sweetheart deal over Busang gold deposit.
- Canada 'slam dunks' U.S. in farm dispute: Panel rules on dairy, poultry products can remain.
- Kevin Benson back as the restructurer: Canadian Airline's rookie boss thought his days of saving companies were over. But his past may be a plus in his bid to rescue the airline.
- Timbuktu shares plunge $23.15: Ore assay fiasco plays out on first day of trading since April.
- Placer wants Busang too: Placer Dome reveals that it bid for the giant Indonesian gold strike before Jakarta told Bre-X to deal with Barrick. But Placer hasn't given up the hunt.
- Takeover speculation intensifies as Suncor shares rise.
